chapters.n: Joseph Smith’s inspired translation begins with the last verse of Matthew 23. Jesus tells the Jewish leaders they will not see Him as the promised Messiah until they welcome Him at His glorious return; the disciples realize He will come again after being exalted.

f.w: Blessed is he who cometh in the name of the Lord

chapters.n: Leaving the temple, the disciples ask Jesus to explain His statement that the temple buildings would be thrown down and left desolate.

f.g: Herod’s temple complex in Jerusalem, a massive and beautiful structure still being expanded in Jesus’s day.

chapters.n: Jesus prophesies that not one stone of the temple will remain on another. This was fulfilled in AD 70 when Roman armies destroyed Jerusalem and its temple.

On the Mount of Olives, overlooking the temple, the disciples privately ask two questions: when will the temple and the Jews be destroyed, and what is the sign of Christ’s coming and the end of the world? The JST makes clear the “end of the world” means the destruction of the wicked.

f.g: A ridge east of Jerusalem across the Kidron Valley, with a full view of the temple mount.

f.w: the destruction of the wicked, which is the end of the world

chapters.n: Jesus’s first warning: don’t let anyone deceive you. Spiritual discernment is the theme of the whole sermon.

f.g: be careful, pay attention.

f.w: Take heed that no man deceive you

chapters.n: Many will come claiming to be Christ or speaking in His name, and many will be misled.
Jesus warns the disciples they will be handed over, persecuted, and killed, and hated by the nations because they follow Him. Most of the Twelve did die as martyrs, according to tradition.
Many will stumble in their faith (“be offended”), betraying and hating one another. Persecution from outside will be matched by division within.

f.g: caused to stumble or fall away from faith.

chapters.n: Many false prophets will arise and lead people astray.
Because wickedness will spread, many people’s love will grow cold — sin erodes the capacity to love.

f.g: grow cold.

f.w: the love of many shall wax cold

chapters.n: Those who stay steadfast and are not overcome will be saved. Endurance is the answer to deception and persecution.

f.g: firm, unwavering.

chapters.n: When the “abomination of desolation” foretold by Daniel comes concerning Jerusalem’s destruction, the disciples should stand in holy places. Historically this points to the Roman desecration of the temple.

f.g: A desecrating horror that brings ruin; first used of an idolatrous profanation of the temple (Daniel 9:27; Daniel 11:31; Daniel 12:11).

chapters.n: When that day comes, those in Judea should flee to the mountains. Early church history records that many Christians escaped the siege of Jerusalem by leaving before it fell.

f.g: The southern region of the land of Israel, including Jerusalem.

chapters.n: Anyone on a roof should flee immediately without going inside to save belongings. Flat roofs were common living spaces, often reached by outside stairs.

f.g: flat roof used for work, rest, and prayer.

chapters.n: A worker in the field shouldn’t even go back for his cloak — escape must be instant.

f.g: Likely the outer cloak, left aside while working.

chapters.n: It will be especially hard for pregnant and nursing mothers who cannot flee quickly. Jesus expresses compassion for the most vulnerable.

f.g: nurse a baby.

f.w: wo unto them that are with child

chapters.n: Pray that your escape won’t be in winter, when travel is hard, or on the Sabbath, when travel was restricted and gates might be closed.

f.g: Jewish custom limited travel on the Sabbath, which would hinder flight.

chapters.n: The tribulation upon the Jews and Jerusalem will be worse than any before or after in Israel’s history. The Roman siege of AD 70 brought famine, slaughter, and the temple’s destruction.
All they have suffered so far is only the beginning of their sorrows.
Unless those days were cut short, no one would survive; but for the sake of the covenant people, they will be shortened. God limits tribulation out of mercy.

f.g: God’s chosen, covenant-keeping people.

chapters.n: Jesus marks a transition: the prophecy about Jerusalem’s destruction is finished. Now He turns to the signs before His Second Coming, beginning with a warning not to believe claims that Christ is “here” or “there.”

f.w: these things I have spoken unto you concerning the Jews
f.g: A JST addition that clearly separates the AD 70 prophecy from the latter-day prophecy.

chapters.n: False Christs and false prophets will perform great signs, deceiving even the elect if that were possible. Miracles alone are not proof of truth.
Jesus gives these warnings for the sake of His covenant people. They will hear of wars and rumors of wars, but they should not be troubled — the end is not yet.

f.w: see that ye be not troubled

chapters.n: Jesus emphasizes that He has warned them in advance, so they can be prepared rather than surprised.
If people say Christ is in the desert or in secret rooms, don’t believe them. His true return will not be hidden.

f.g: inner rooms — hidden places.

chapters.n: Christ’s coming will be as unmistakable as dawn spreading from east to west across the whole earth. The JST changes “lightning” to “the light of the morning.”

f.g: Matthew 24:27 (KJV) reads “as the lightning cometh out of the east.”

chapters.n: A proverb: where a carcass lies, eagles (or vultures) gather. The JST applies this to the gathering of the elect from all parts of the earth — drawn to Christ as surely as birds to food.

f.g: Greek aetoi, which can also mean vultures.

f.w: gathered from the four quarters of the earth

chapters.n: Repeating an earlier sign, Jesus says His latter-day people will also hear of wars and rumors of wars.
Nations and kingdoms will fight one another, with famines, plagues, and earthquakes in many places.

f.g: various, different.
deadly epidemics.

chapters.n: The latter days will repeat the pattern: wickedness will chill love, but whoever is not overcome will be saved.

f.w: he that shall not be overcome

chapters.n: The gospel will be preached to all nations as a witness before the end — the destruction of the wicked. Latter-day Saints see worldwide missionary work as fulfilling this sign.

f.w: this Gospel of the Kingdom shall be preached in all the world

chapters.n: Daniel’s “abomination of desolation” will be fulfilled again in the last days. The JST shows the prophecy has two fulfillments — one in AD 70 (verse 12) and another before the Second Coming.
After that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, the moon give no light, and stars fall — cosmic signs that announce the Lord’s coming.
The generation that sees these signs will not pass away until all is fulfilled. The JST clarifies that this refers to the generation in which the signs appear.

f.g: JST adds “in which these things shall be shown forth,” pointing to the latter-day generation.

chapters.n: Heaven and earth will someday pass away, but Christ’s words never will — every promise will be fulfilled.

f.w: my words shall not pass away

chapters.n: Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, all tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see Christ coming in the clouds with power and great glory.

f.w: the sign of the Son of Man
coming in the clouds of heaven, with power and great glory

chapters.n: A key JST addition: whoever treasures up Christ’s word will not be deceived. Christ will send angels with a great trumpet to gather His remaining elect from everywhere.

f.w: whoso treasureth up my word, shall not be deceived
f.g: This promise is not in Matthew 24; Joseph Smith’s translation adds it.

f.w: the great sound of a trumpet

chapters.n: Jesus teaches through the fig tree: when its branches turn tender and leaves appear, you know summer is close. Signs show the season even if not the exact date.

f.w: a parable of the fig tree

chapters.n: Likewise, when the elect see these signs, they will know Christ’s coming is near — “at the doors.”
No one knows the exact day or hour — not even the angels — only the Father. Attempts to set dates miss the point of watching.

f.w: of that day, and hour, no one knoweth

chapters.n: The days before Christ’s coming will be like Noah’s days before the Flood.

f.w: as it was in the days of Noah

chapters.n: People before the Flood went about ordinary life — eating, drinking, marrying — right up until Noah entered the ark. The problem was not ordinary life but ignoring God’s warnings.

f.w: eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage

chapters.n: They didn’t realize anything was wrong until the Flood swept them away. Christ’s coming will catch the unprepared just as suddenly.

f.w: knew not until the flood came

chapters.n: In the last days two people may be working in the same field: one taken, the other left. Outward circumstances will be the same; inner preparation will differ.

f.w: the one shall be taken, and the other left

chapters.n: Two women grinding grain at a hand mill — one taken, the other left. Grinding at the mill was daily household labor.

f.g: Turning a hand-mill of two stones to make flour, typically women’s daily work.

chapters.n: Jesus applies His words to everyone: watch, because you don’t know the hour your Lord will come.

f.w: what I say unto one, I say unto all

f.g: stay alert and spiritually awake.

chapters.n: If a homeowner knew when a thief would come, he would stay awake and protect his house. Christ will come unexpectedly, like a thief in the night, to those not watching.

f.g: The night was divided into “watches” (time periods of guard duty).
allowed.
broken into.

chapters.n: So be ready — the Son of Man will come when you least expect Him.
Jesus asks: who is the faithful and wise servant whom the master puts in charge of feeding his household on time? Faithfulness means caring for others while the master is away.

f.g: food at the proper time.

chapters.n: Blessed is the servant found doing his duty when the master returns; he will be made ruler over everything the master has.
But an evil servant tells himself the master is delaying his return. Assuming there is plenty of time breeds neglect.
That servant starts abusing his fellow servants and partying with drunkards — the behavior of someone who no longer expects accountability.

f.g: strike, beat.

chapters.n: The master will return on a day and hour the servant isn’t expecting.

f.w: in an hour that he is not aware of

chapters.n: The master will punish him severely and assign him a place with the hypocrites, where there is weeping and grinding of teeth — images of regret and anguish.

f.g: cut him in two — a vivid image of severe punishment.

chapters.n: So the wicked will come to their end, as Moses prophesied — cut off from the people. But the end of the earth itself is still in the future. This JST verse adds a final clarification not found in Matthew.

f.w: according to the prophecy of Moses

f.g: later on, in due time.
